info.title: Armada shared control API
info.description: Generated integration REST contracts. Includes SDK operations, launch discovery (launch/options, golden/list) and shared-tool routes. sandbox/launch accepts a golden launch or a Docker launch. Administrative and provider-specific extensions are outside this description. Files use sandbox/exec; this description does not assert provider availability.

post.description: Gives the agent its next instruction as a new turn. Without conversation_id the first send of an idle sandbox opens a conversation and later sends continue the latest one. To redirect a turn that is still running, use steer. The turn runs with the model and effort chosen at launch; model and reasoning_effort override them for this turn only. Experimental runtime follow-up requires request_id, an empty ready sandbox, existing conversation, or verified empty checkpoint; retained idle pauses wake automatically before expiry. Preserved stopped Boat/Modal sandboxes resume on send; terminal sandboxes refuse controls with recovery guidance. Model/effort remain pinned to launch.

post.description: Forks a golden into a new sandbox, pulls its repos, runs its init commands, and starts the agent. With `prompt` the agent starts working at once (status running). Without it the sandbox is left ready and the conversation starts at the first `send`. The sandbox gets only your (or your org's) Armada credentials for this agent, never the boat.dev account's. When the caller connected GitHub, git and gh in the sandbox act as that person (8 hour token): see `github` in the answer. Setup can take a few minutes. Docker hosts use the second request variant: provider "docker" with no golden. launch/options reports each provider's launch sources.

post.description: The agent's events oldest first: prompts (with status and failure reason), messages and tool calls, steers. The default is one bounded page (100 events). Set all to read every available page (up to 100 pages) in one response. Pass the returned cursor as cursor to read only what is new. An event read twice has the same id and the newer body; each id appears once per response.
